issues.title: Table designer type system is too narrow to represent real-world SQLite schemas
issues.recommendation: Define how the designer handles arbitrary SQLite declared types. Recommended: make

a freeform text field (persisted verbatim into DDL) with an optional affinity dropdown/helper (INTEGER/REAL/TEXT/BLOB/NUMERIC/NONE). For existing tables, always display the exact declared type string (e.g.,
) and never coerce it to the small enum. Add explicit v1 scope text: what happens when a column has a type outside the affinity set, and what type strings are allowed/blocked in the UI (if any).
issues.acceptanceTest: E2E checklist: (1) Import DB containing columns declared as
. (2) Open table designer; verify displayed type strings match exactly what is in sqlite_master/PRAGMA table_info. (3) Add a column with custom type
. (4) Perform a rename-column operation; verify all unaffected columns preserve their original declared type strings.

issues.title: Export + IndexedDB close/switch semantics are underspecified and can cause silent data loss
issues.evidence: Download Database" button exports the full `.sqlite` file
The full database is serialized and stored as a blob in IndexedDB.
Debounced — saves are batched with a 500ms debounce after the last SQLite write.
Expanding a non-active DB switches the active DB (closes the current one, opens the selected one).
issues.recommendation: Make the snapshot/consistency contract explicit for (A) database export and (B) IndexedDB mode when switching/closing. Concretely: (1) Export MUST be generated via SQLite's backup mechanism (e.g., sqlite3_backup or VACUUM INTO) to produce a transactionally consistent file independent of journal mode, rather than copying the raw OPFS file bytes. (2) In IndexedDB mode, switching away from an active DB MUST flush any pending debounced snapshot and await IndexedDB commit before disposing the in-memory SQLite instance (show
and block the switch until done, or offer a cancel/force-discard path with explicit confirmation). Add an E2E test for fast switch-within-debounce to ensure no loss.
issues.acceptanceTest: E2E + CLI verification: (1) Force IndexedDB mode; edit a cell; immediately (within <200ms) switch to another DB; switch back or hard refresh; verify the edit persists. (2) Export consistency: make a write, export, then open the exported file in a fresh SQLite process and verify the latest write exists (e.g., `sqlite3 exported.sqlite "SELECT ..."` returns the new row). (3) While an in-flight UI edit exists, attempt export/switch: verify the app either (a) forces commit explicitly and documents it, or (b) prompts to commit/discard/cancel, and behavior matches the documented contract.

issues.title: Visual query builder WHERE/join semantics are too underspecified to be testable
issues.recommendation: Specify the exact v1 grammar the builder supports: allowed operators (=, !=, <, <=, >, >=, LIKE contains, STARTS WITH, ENDS WITH, IS NULL/IS NOT NULL), AND/OR grouping rules (if any), parameterization policy (recommended: generated SQL uses placeholders and a parameter list, not raw interpolation), value typing (number vs string vs NULL), and join condition limitations (recommended: equality joins only via drag between columns). Update E2E-US-006-01 to assert an exact SQL string (or an AST snapshot) rather than a loose
issues.acceptanceTest: Unit + E2E: (1) Given a builder config, SQL generator outputs deterministic SQL + ordered params. (2) Build WHERE with a string containing quotes and `%` and verify it executes correctly without breaking SQL. (3) Build an IS NULL condition and verify correct SQL. (4) Build a RIGHT JOIN and ensure generated SQL qualifies columns to avoid ambiguity when column names collide.

issues.title: Rebuild dependency detection relies on an ambiguous sqlite_master “reference scan”
issues.recommendation: means and make it robust/testable. Recommendation: after any schema rebuild, compile-check ALL user-defined SQL objects from sqlite_master (views/triggers) via prepare/EXPLAIN to catch breakage, rather than trying to pre-filter by a potentially lossy string scan. Then surface a dependency error listing the failing objects. If pre-flight warnings are desired, define them as best-effort and state explicitly they may not find every dependency.
issues.acceptanceTest: E2E: Create dependencies with tricky SQL (quoted identifiers, schema-qualified names, different casing, comments). Drop/rename a column and verify the rebuild is rolled back and the error list includes the exact failing view/trigger SQL. Additionally verify that objects not obviously
a naive string scan are still caught by the post-rebuild compile check.

issues.title: CSP spec is likely incomplete for workers/PWA bundling and meta-tag CSP has known limitations
issues.recommendation: Explicitly define CSP delivery and required directives for the chosen build output. Recommended: require CSP as an HTTP response header in production (not only meta), add `worker-src 'self'` (and `blob:` if bundler emits blob URL workers), and include an explicit test for
while loading WASM + workers. If clickjacking protection matters, note that `frame-ancestors` should be enforced via header in production deployments.
issues.acceptanceTest: Checklist: (1) Run the production build with CSP enabled; verify the app loads, workers start, WASM loads, and there are zero CSP violations in the console. (2) Verify the app cannot be embedded in an iframe in production deployment (if frame-ancestors is a requirement). (3) Run E2E-SEC-01 under CSP and ensure it still passes.

issues.title: Read-only enforcement in multi-tab mode needs an explicit “writes are blocked everywhere” contract
issues.recommendation: Add a single, explicit rule: when in read-only mode, ALL write entry points are disabled and any attempted write returns a consistent error (grid edits, table designer apply, ERD FK changes, import, and SQL editor DML/DDL). Also specify whether the SQLite connection is opened with read-only flags (preferred) versus UI-only gating, and how errors appear if a write is attempted (banner + toast + inline error).
issues.acceptanceTest: E2E: Open same DB in two tabs; in the second tab attempt (1) grid cell edit, (2) CREATE TABLE in SQL editor, (3) import CSV append. Verify each is blocked with the same read-only error, and verify the first tab’s DB content remains unchanged after the second tab attempts.

issues.title: Behavior for databases larger than stated targets is undefined in OPFS mode
issues.evidence: . Fallback contract specifies >50MB warning in IndexedDB mode, but OPFS mode has no >100MB rule.
issues.recommendation: Add an explicit policy for >100MB in OPFS mode: either (A) allow with a warning and no perf guarantees, or (B) block with a clear message and suggest desktop tooling. Also specify whether the 100MB cap applies to import only, or also to databases that grow past 100MB via edits/imports.
issues.acceptanceTest: E2E: Attempt to import a 150MB DB in OPFS mode. Verify the app shows the documented warning/blocking message, remains responsive (no crash), and does not partially import (either completes successfully if allowed, or aborts cleanly if blocked).

issues.title: Ctrl+S shortcut is ambiguous in an auto-persisting app
issues.recommendation: Clarify and standardize what Ctrl+S does per storage mode. Suggested v1: Ctrl+S triggers

(export) and never implies a manual save (since OPFS mode is auto-durable). Document whether default browser 'Save Page' is prevented and ensure the action is discoverable in the UI (tooltip/command palette/help).
issues.acceptanceTest: Manual + E2E: Press Ctrl+S with a DB open; verify the documented action happens (export dialog/download flow) and the browser does not open its default save-page UI. Repeat in IndexedDB mode and verify consistent behavior.

suggestions.title: Define a single versioned metadata model for per-DB + global state
suggestions.description: You already have ERD sidecar JSON and several implied settings (FK enforcement toggle, query history, storage usage indicator). A unified, versioned metadata spec prevents drift and migration pain.
suggestions.recommendation: section describing: (1) per-DB metadata file(s) (e.g., `<db>.meta.json` containing ERD positions, last opened, UI state), (2) global settings storage (e.g., `settings_v1` in IndexedDB/localStorage), and (3) migration rules (version field, unknown-key preservation, upgrade path).
suggestions.rationale: Reduces future refactors and makes persistence behavior testable and predictable across OPFS and IndexedDB modes.

suggestions.title: Add a clear UX contract for “dirty state” across the whole app
suggestions.description: There are multiple dirty-state concepts: in-flight cell edits, pending IndexedDB snapshot, schema changes pending apply, and read-only mode. Users need consistent cues and consistent navigation prompts.
suggestions.recommendation: (committed to SQLite but not yet snapshotted in IndexedDB mode), (3)
(read-only/quota). Define exact banners/status texts and when navigation is blocked vs warned.
suggestions.rationale: Prevents accidental writes, prevents accidental loss in fallback mode, and makes E2E scenarios deterministic.

suggestions.title: FK creation helper when parent column is not UNIQUE/PK
suggestions.description: SQLite requires referenced parent columns to be PRIMARY KEY or have a UNIQUE index. Drag-to-create FK will often hit this, and the current PRD doesn’t describe the UX.
suggestions.recommendation: On FK creation failure due to missing uniqueness, show a targeted dialog:
Offer one-click creation of a UNIQUE index on the parent column (with previewed DDL) before retrying FK creation.
suggestions.rationale: Turns a confusing constraint error into a guided workflow and reduces failed attempts in the ERD.

suggestions.title: Add cancel/timeout patterns for long-running SQL and schema operations
suggestions.description: Import/export have cancel, but ad-hoc queries (e.g., accidental CROSS JOIN) and rebuilds can still hang the UI and create “is it frozen?” moments.
suggestions.recommendation: Add a cancel button for query execution and schema rebuild operations (worker-side interrupt if supported, or cooperative cancellation between statements). Also add a
status with elapsed time and row fetch progress for large results.
suggestions.rationale: Improves perceived performance and resilience without changing core scope.

suggestions.title: Make identifier handling explicit and uniform everywhere
suggestions.description: The PRD mentions quoting identifiers in generators, but many surfaces depend on it: sidebar, query builder, designer, grid filters, and error displays.
suggestions.recommendation: subsection: always quote with double quotes, escape embedded quotes, preserve exact casing for display, and define a canonical
used only for collision checks (case-insensitive). Add fixtures with reserved words and weird characters to lock it in.
suggestions.rationale: Prevents subtle breakage on real-world DBs and reduces security/escaping surprises.

suggestions.title: Consider hiding RIGHT JOIN behind an “Advanced” toggle in v1
suggestions.description: RIGHT JOIN is uncommon for the target users and adds UX surface area (especially for visual join directionality).
suggestions.recommendation: Default the builder to INNER and LEFT joins; keep RIGHT JOIN supported by the engine but gate the UI control behind an “Advanced” toggle, or defer it to v1.1 if it complicates the canvas UX.
suggestions.rationale: Reduces cognitive load and UI complexity while keeping the core benefit (joins) intact.

suggestions.title: Add a “diagnostics export” (local-only) for debugging test failures
suggestions.description: You already plan perf traces/JSON artifacts in CI. A similar concept for user-reported issues (without telemetry) improves supportability.
suggestions.recommendation: action that packages: app version, storage mode, feature flags, recent error logs, and (optionally) a redacted schema dump (sqlite_master only). Never auto-send; just download a file the user can choose to share.
suggestions.rationale: Supports debugging while respecting the no-telemetry constraint.

strengths: Very strong v1 scope discipline: explicit non-goals plus clear per-feature “supported vs not supported” boundaries (especially in table designer and query builder).
Acceptance criteria are unusually concrete and implementation-friendly, with many E2E IDs that map directly to Playwright scenarios.
Persistence architecture is thoughtfully separated into OPFS direct durability vs IndexedDB snapshot fallback, including quota handling and multi-tab locking strategy.
Performance targets are measurable (time, heap limits, frame time) and paired with a CI measurement approach (CDP heap sampling, traces, fixture generator).
Data interchange rules are precise and testable, especially the NULL vs empty-string CSV semantics and JSON null handling.
Security model is well-considered for a no-backend app (DOM escaping, CSP intent, parameterized queries, worker isolation) and includes a concrete security E2E test.
The ERD feature has a crisp metadata schema with versioning and forward-compat preservation, which is exactly the right pattern for long-lived local data.

overallAssessment.summary: This PRD is close to implementation-ready with strong acceptance criteria, testing hooks, and a solid offline/persistence story. Address the two major gaps (type declaration handling and consistent snapshot/export + IndexedDB switch/close durability) to avoid schema incompatibilities and silent data loss.
